_comment: General kinds of sub-recipe, and the names each goes by. A recipe whose title ends in one of the names ('All-Buttah Pie Dough', 'Golden Cheese Rough Puff Pastry') or is one ('Pâte Brisée') is of that kind. In matching, having any name of a kind ('pie crust') covers a sub-recipe of that kind, with a note, and a reference written as a kind ('9-inch pie crust (see Recommended Crusts)') can be made with any of the book's recipes of that kind. Names are compared without accents, case or plurals. Only list names that mean the same thing to a cook; a graham crust is not a pie dough.
